name: Soldier
description:
They outnumber you three to one and they're coming on fast. You give a shout, rallying your allies to your side: if you're going to survive this, it's going to be back-to-back, shields up. Remembering your training, you plant the haft of your polearm against the ground just in front of your back foot, shift your weight forward, and bring your shield up just below your eyes. You feel the fear in those around you and remember how you felt in your first battle. Drawing hope from deep within, you shout a few inspiring words, clashing your blade against your shield for emphasis. You feel them stand firmer at your side. You're a unit now. If the line holds, then you'll find the next chance, and the next, until you find victory, however improbable.

A Soldier is a Soldier, plain and simple. Bravery, humility, benefit of the collective over the self - these are the principles they live by, complimented by a broad range of combative skill that allows them to make themselves useful in any situation that arises. They may not be the strongest, fastest or the most clever, but when they rally their allies around them, they become the most formidable fighting unit on the battlefield.

The Soldier mestiere uses Hope and their allies as a resource. You gain defensive and offensive bonuses by sticking together and flanking your enemies. You accumulate MP via the Momentum ability as you take down foes, and can also convert Hope into MP. You can spend that MP on abilities that amplify your own combative skills or, more often, put you in harm's way in order to grant benefits to your allies. You have the broadest martial training in the game, and if worst comes to worst, A Good Death allows your memory to help your friends after you've fallen in honor.

Soldier rewards a careful, selfless, tactical approach to combat, with a broad range of tools in your tool belt allowing you to react to every shift of the battlefield.

Play a Soldier if you want to:

  • Master a wide range of weapons of armor, bringing the trained competence of a professional soldier to bear regardless of what the fight demands.

  • Make everyone around you more effective, turning proximity into a tactical advantage and each enemy's defeat into fuel for the next clash.

  • Embrace sacrifice as a strategy, understanding that sometimes the best way to win a battle is to give something up.

Questions to consider when making a Soldier:

  • Under whom did they serve, and what does that service mean to them now—duty still owed, a past left behind, or the only life they've ever known how to live?

  • Do they carry the habit of acting as a unit in their life off the battlefield? Does their selflessness extend to all parts of their life, or does duty and danger transform them?

  • Has their loyalty or sense of duty ever been tested, taken for granted or abused? Depending on collective strength us making yourself vulnerable. Has that ever come back to the bite them?

  • What is their relationship to the idea of an honorable death? Is it something they yearn for, something they fear, or something they don't think about at all?

  • Were they ever in a fight they knew they couldn't win? What did they do? How has it shaped them?

novizio.description: You have received basic military training and have at least some experience on the battlefield, fighting as part of a unit of an army.
novizio.gratuiti: A woolen blanket, a shallow bowl and spoon. A small reminder of home.
